synopsis: IEC 61508 is described as the seven-part parent standard for electrical, electronic and programmable safety systems across industries, defining functional safety through correct responses to inputs and faults [f15268, f11991]. Its Safety Integrity Levels range from SIL 1 to SIL 4; for frequently acting functions, SIL 1 permits a dangerous-failure probability band of one per 100,000 to one per million hours [f12050, f12051]. Chapter 10 presents proven in use as a compliance route for reused elements, requiring identical or highly similar elements and use conditions plus justified service history; the glossary adds sufficiently few failures to support a statistical claim [f7933, f7934, f12351]. IEC 61508 practice reportedly demands higher confidence than the 70% used in the ISO 26262 formula, but proven in use does not validate a simulator, and adding automatic braking changes the item relative to the fielded warning system [f7936, f14926]. For planning, IEC 61508 remains an alternative whose status and fit were not verified, and neither its off-line tool classes T1–T3 nor its proven-in-use provisions were verified in detail [f2354, f12054, f10544, f15271].
